evals.name: tooltip-as-fix-pushback
evals.prompt: Users keep getting confused by our 'Archive' button on the dashboard -- they think it deletes the item. Let's just add a tooltip explaining what it does.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on the tooltip as the fix, framing it as a workaround rather than a solution, and proposes fixing the actual affordance (clearer label, icon, or confirmation copy that distinguishes archive from delete) instead of relying on hover text that a first-time user won't see before clicking.

assertions.text: Explicitly frames adding a tooltip as a workaround/deferral rather than accepting it as the resolution
Proposes a concrete alternative fix to the affordance itself (e.g. clearer label, different icon, or in-context confirmation text) rather than only the tooltip
Notes that a tooltip requires hovering before the mistake happens, which doesn't prevent the confusion it's meant to address
Does not simply agree to add the tooltip and move on

evals.name: custom-dropdown-accessibility-gap
evals.prompt: Here's our custom dropdown component: a <div> with an onClick handler that shows/hides a list of <div> options below it, styled to look like a select. Any concerns?
evals.expected_output: Flags multiple concrete gaps: no keyboard support (can't be opened/navigated via keyboard), missing ARIA roles/attributes (should announce as a listbox/combobox with expanded state), and no focus management (focus doesn't move into the option list or return to the trigger on close) -- rather than only commenting on visual styling.

assertions.text: Identifies that a <div> with onClick has no built-in keyboard support (can't be triggered by Enter/Space, no arrow-key navigation)
Identifies the missing ARIA role/state (e.g. should behave like a listbox or combobox with an expanded/collapsed state exposed)
Raises a focus management concern (focus should move into the option list when opened and/or return to the trigger when closed)
Recommends a concrete remediation (native <select>/<button> where possible, or proper ARIA + keyboard handling for the custom version) rather than only listing problems

evals.name: tabindex-hack-flagged
evals.prompt: Our form fields are visually out of order on the page for layout reasons, so we set tabindex values like 1, 2, 3, 4 manually on each field to fix the tab order. Does that work?
evals.expected_output: Flags the use of positive tabindex values as a fragile anti-pattern, explains it overrides natural DOM order and becomes a maintenance liability as the page changes, and recommends reordering the underlying DOM/source order (with CSS used for the visual layout) instead of manual tabindex numbering.

assertions.text: Identifies positive tabindex values (1, 2, 3...) as an anti-pattern rather than confirming it's a good solution
Explains the maintenance/fragility risk of manual tabindex numbers as the page evolves
Recommends fixing DOM/source order and using CSS for visual positioning instead of tabindex hacks
Does not simply validate the tabindex 1/2/3/4 approach as correct

evals.name: color-only-status-indicator
evals.prompt: We show order status as a colored dot next to each row -- green means shipped, yellow means processing, red means delayed. Good to ship?
evals.expected_output: Flags this as a color-only accessibility gap (fails for colorblind users and anyone not perceiving color, and violates WCAG's 'don't rely on color alone' principle) and recommends adding a second signal such as an icon, text label, or pattern alongside the color.

assertions.text: Identifies that using color alone to convey status is an accessibility problem, not just a nice-to-have improvement
References the specific issue (e.g. colorblind users, or WCAG's use-of-color guidance) rather than a vague 'consider accessibility' comment
Recommends a concrete second signal (icon, text label, or pattern) in addition to color
Does not approve shipping as-is without raising this gap

evals.name: first-run-empty-state-design
evals.prompt: We're building a new 'Projects' page. When a brand-new user signs up, the page will just show an empty table with column headers and no rows. Is that fine for launch?
evals.expected_output: Flags that a bare empty table fails the self-narration bar for a first-time user (no indication of what to do next) and recommends a designed empty state that explains the page is empty because no projects exist yet and surfaces the create-a-project action directly, rather than leaving the user to infer the next step from column headers alone.

assertions.text: Identifies that a bare empty table doesn't meet the zero-onboarding/self-narration bar for a first-time user
Distinguishes this as a genuinely-empty first-run state (not a filtered or error state) and asks for or proposes a specific empty-state message for that case
Recommends surfacing the primary action (e.g. 'create your first project') directly within the empty state, not just relying on the user to find a button elsewhere
Does not approve the bare empty table as sufficient for launch without raising this
